CARES Requirements Traceability

Status key: Prototype means code exists as an incomplete, non-production demonstration. Planned means documented target work. Not implemented means no corresponding working product feature exists. These classifications describe current implementation, not requirement approval. Rows sourced from the Architecture Review identify proposed design requirements; numeric performance assumptions remain unapproved until the owner accepts them.

Test evidence and limitations

The existing suite consists of five unittest cases in tests/test_cares_core.py. It covers a narrow local demonstration: repeated identical stable identity across three source IDs, sequential quota rejection, same-tenant/cross-tenant behavior of the helper predicate, AI classification blocking, and disabled-AI status. Passing these tests does not establish persistence, concurrency correctness, external transmission privacy, database tenant isolation, secure authentication, or production readiness.

Target acceptance criteria are listed in the DEVELOPMENT_ROADMAP.md, THREAT_MODEL.md, and DATA_ARCHITECTURE.md.

Proposed performance assumptions (not confirmed requirements)

The following initial capacity figures were introduced for planning and require owner approval: up to 10 tenants / 5,000 active assets; 25 EPS sustained aggregate and 100 EPS for a five-minute burst; 1 KiB average and 256 KiB maximum event; 30-day event retention; 25 EPS ingest acknowledgment p95 <=1 second / p99 <=3 seconds; worker throughput >=150 EPS; accepted-to-detection p95 <=30 seconds / p99 <=60 seconds; outbox p95 lag <30 seconds. Hardware, realistic event distribution, retention/legal requirements, and all test evidence remain to be agreed/validated. See DEVELOPMENT_ROADMAP.md, DATA_ARCHITECTURE.md, and ADR 0005.
